summary: NFP June 2026 (57K, vs 114K consensus) triggered two stops on July 2 — long-MU (Apple/CXMT/YMTC mobile DRAM sourcing killed the memory demand thesis, -11.5%) and short-MSFT (Warsh hike probability collapsed, rate-relief trade lifted MSFT above stop, -5.9%) — while GD hit Target 1 at $362 on July 1 (+7.0%). US markets closed today (July 4 observed); three new ideas generated for the reopening July 7: META long re-entry at the $583 post-T1 pullback, AMD short on NFP growth-scare distribution, and AMZN long on AWS defensive quality + rate-relief re-rating. TSLA $392.24 sits just $2.24 above its $390 stop — monitor closely on the July 7 open. SPCX Nasdaq-100 inclusion ($7.3B forced buying) on July 7 is the dominant near-term catalyst for the active slate.

closed_today.note: Target 1 hit at $362 on July 1; GD extended to $373.54 on July 2. 40% of position taken at T1 per plan; remaining 60% can hold toward T2 ($385) and T3 ($415) as DOD supplemental and NDAA FY2027 catalysts develop.

Apple sourcing deals with CXMT and YMTC for mobile DRAM (announced July 1-2) triggered a memory complex selloff. MU closed $975.56 on July 2 — breaching both the $1,000 half-cut trigger and the $990 two-session stop floor in a single session, warranting full exit.

NFP 57K collapsed Warsh July hike probability to near zero. MSFT was best large-cap tech +1.69% on rate relief, closing $390.79 and breaching the $388 stop on the first trading session. Created and stopped in the same day.
